title: Config Risk Assessor for batching/caching automation
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Build a lightweight automated service (Config Risk Assessor) that evaluates proposed batching and KV-cache configuration changes and produces a pass/fail score plus a rollback recommendation. The assessor should run a prioritized set of anchor prompts and statistical checks to detect quality regressions tied to cost-driven optimizations, and integrate into the existing apply/rollback pipeline (canary -> auto-apply).
background: Our autotune and recommendation engine has reduced token cost but has a small number of customer-visible regressions that slipped past current acceptance checks. Current safety gates rely on broad eval suites that are too slow for fast applies. We need a fast, conservative assessor that provides actionable risk signals (scorecards) before a config is applied to production or promoted from canary.
scope:
- Implement an assessor microservice that accepts proposed config diffs and returns structured risk outputs (score, failure reasons, recommended mitigation).
- Run a compact 'anchor prompt' set (200-500 samples) weighted by production traffic buckets.
- Compute statistical checks (paired test / bootstrap for quality metrics) and cost/latency deltas.
- Integrate with canary rollout pipeline to block or allow automated promotion and to trigger safe rollback when thresholds breach.
- Produce human-readable runbook snippets to help on-call triage.
out_of_scope:
- Full regression harnesses and large-scale offline evals (these remain part of extensive nightly jobs).
- UI console changes; we will emit events to existing rollout dashboards handled by a separate ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Assessor returns a deterministic JSON scorecard for a config diff within 90s for typical Canary sample sizes.
Anchor prompt suite detects injected regressions of >=5% quality drop (measured by primary metric) with >90% power at alpha=0.01 on synthetic tests.
Automated canary promotion is blocked when risk_score >= 0.7 or when any critical metric regresses beyond configured thresholds.
Rollback reason messages include the top-3 contributing signals (e.g., response_length_imbalance, embedding_similarity_drop, latency_tail_increase).
Operational run must include telemetry events that surface cost delta, latency delta, sample counts, and p-values to the Console and alerts channel.
implementation_notes: Create a lightweight anchor prompt corpus by sampling high-QPS routes and deduplicating by embedding similarity (using existing embedding service).
Primary quality metric: route-specific semantic similarity (cosine) measured against model baseline answers rather than token-level metrics; fallback to n-gram overlap for short responses.
Use stratified paired bootstrap to estimate confidence intervals for metric deltas; compute one-sided p-values for regression directionality.
Scorecard fields: baseline_metric, candidate_metric, delta_pct, p_value, cost_delta_pct, latency_tail_95_delta_ms, sample_size, risk_score (0-1), verdict (pass|fail|manual_review).

Risk scoring heuristic: weighted combination of effect size normalized by variance, cost savings magnitude, and latency SLO violations. Heuristic params stored in config and tunable via feature flags.
Implement a 'conservative mode' that increases sensitivity (lowers thresholds) for high-customer-impact routes and enterprise tenants.
test_plan: Unit tests for assessor scoring logic and edge cases (zero-variance, small sample sizes).
Synthetic injection tests: run anchor corpus with controlled perturbations (semantic swaps, hallucination injection) to benchmark detection power.
A/B pilot: shadow assessor on 4 production canaries for 2 weeks and compare assessor verdicts to nightly full evals to calibrate thresholds.
Statistical parameters: target power >= 0.9 for 5% effect, alpha=0.01 for primary checks; minimum sample size 200 per canary (configurable).
Backfill historical config changes and verify assessor would have caught at least 90% of previously known regressions identified by manual eval.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow): deploy assessor in shadow for canary traffic, log scorecards, no automated blocking. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (manual gate): surface assessor verdicts in PR and Console; require explicit PM/Eng approval for auto-promotion. Duration: 1 sprint.
Phase 3 (soft auto-block): auto-block promotions on risk_score >= 0.9 or critical signal; send automated alerts to on-call. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 4 (full auto-apply with auto-rollback): enable auto-apply for low-risk configs and auto-rollback on post-apply metric breaches for eligible routes. Release guardrails enabled by default.
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose metrics: assessor_latency_seconds, assessor_sample_count, risk_score_histogram, blocked_promotions_total, post_apply_regressions_total.
Alert if assessor_latency_seconds > 120s for >1% of runs or if blocked_promotions_total spikes >3x baseline in 1h.
Create a dashboard card showing canary-by-canary scorecards and recent rollbacks with root-cause tags.
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting. Decided anchor prompt approach and prioritized routes: chat/conversation, summarization, and search-rewrite.
2025-01-18: Prototype of paired bootstrap implemented by @Liam Chen; initial power estimate shows 85% at n=200 for 7% effect — need n=350 for 5% effect.
2025-01-24: Reviewed with PM and Product QA. Agreed to add conservative mode for enterprise tenants and to include cost delta as an explicit factor in risk_score.
2025-01-29: Integration spec drafted; added event schema for Console and alerting channels (link in artifacts).
2025-02-01: Shadow deployed to two canaries; first shadow runs completed. Early signal shows one false positive tied to stochastic sampling; tuning in progress.
